changes: Funding turned: free cash flow negative $2.12bn (first negative quarter in the five quarters reviewed) and net debt ~$1.2bn; capex was 106% of operating cash flow.

Meta created a non-voting Class C stock for capital raising, among other purposes (also employee compensation, acquisitions, general corporate purposes) (effective 19 Jan 2027): equity is now a named funding source for compute.

Off-balance-sheet obligations jumped again: leases not yet commenced $355.7bn (+$76.7bn QoQ, 3.4x year-end), non-cancelable commitments $454.5bn (+$105.2bn; mostly third-party cloud), maximum RVG $41.5bn after the El Paso (Texas) JV.
New lease and commitment categories: 'energy-related infrastructure' and 'energy service agreements for data centers' now appear in the notes; Meta is contracting power as well as halls.
Inference economics moved centre stage: Muse is 'very compute intensive'; management targets >10x cost efficiency within a year and wants to sell 'high margin inference'.

consensus_thesis: Ads compounding in the mid-to-high 20s % fund an AI build that can run hot without hurting AA- credit; the stock trades on the size of the 2027 capex number.
headline: The consensus view should shift from 'cash-funded build' to 'externally funded build': long-term ad compounding holds, but Meta is now a net borrower with ~$825bn of off-balance-sheet commitments (gross, components may overlap: uncommenced leases, purchase commitments, contingent cloud) and an equity tool for capex, so credit quality is weakening at the margin.
kona: Meta still guides capacity tight through 2027. It is signing 'energy service agreements' and leasing 'energy-related infrastructure', so power bundled with compute is now something a hyperscaler contracts for. Kona can pitch power as an energy service contract, not only as land plus a hall. The structures to copy are short initial terms (4 years) with a residual value guarantee, and a buyer who backstops capacity it resells. Meta's cost of capital is rising, so Kona should expect investment-grade buyers to push risk onto the developer through short terms and RVG caps, and should price debt on the tenant's credit, not the asset.
monitor: 4Q26 call (late January 2027): 2027 capex and expense guide vs ~$193-205bn street range.
Any Class C issuance, new bond deal or third JV/SPV; pricing vs the April 2026 curve (T+53 to T+147bp).
4Q26 FCF (implied 4Q capex $49-59bn vs ~$33bn quarterly operating cash flow) and the New Mexico appeal bond.

sections.title: KPI dashboard

sections.body: 2026 capex range by quarter: $115-135bn (Jan), $125-145bn (Apr, memory pricing), $130-145bn (Jul), $135-145bn (Oct). The low end has been raised three times in a row. In January management said cash generation would fund 2026 and flagged a 'positive net debt balance' as possible eventually. Both are now playing out. Credibility: Stable (it was telegraphed), but the guidance has risked upward every quarter. Underlying economic performance: strong revenue, with weaker cash conversion. Ex-charge operating income rose 11% YoY while free cash flow went negative, so earnings power holds and the funding burden has moved to the balance sheet.
sections.title: Guidance

sections.body: 5-10 year view: Meta's moat in ads is intact and AI-enhanced. Its moat as a compute owner rests on cheap capital, and that edge is narrowing as it becomes a net borrower with growing guarantees. The 4-year initial terms on JV campuses keep an exit option, but the RVGs mean Meta still bears the residual-value risk.

sections.title: Major risks

sections.body: What the next dollar costs: the April 2026 $25bn deal priced at 4.55% (2031, T+53bp) to 6.45% (2066, T+147bp), Aa3/AA-. The November 2025 $30bn notes priced at 4.20-5.75% coupons. Meta's 5-year CDS hit a record 108bp in October 2026 (single source). No dated secondary spreads were found for 21-22 October. Maturities in the next 24 months are small: $2.75bn in 2027 and $1.5bn in 2028. The pressure is the run-rate gap: 4Q26 implied capex of $49-59bn against ~$33bn quarterly OCF, plus $121.4bn of commitments due in 2027. Off-balance-sheet support: Louisiana (Hyperion; Blue Owl funds 80%, ~$27bn cost, lease from 2029) and Texas/El Paso (~$14bn, lease from 2028) JVs. Each has a 4-year initial lease (renewals to 20 years) plus an RVG; maximum exposure is $68.40bn (equity $4.73bn, leases $18.48bn, funding $3.70bn, RVG $41.49bn). There is also a $10.80bn escrow under infrastructure purchase agreements and $1.53bn of letters of credit. Per share: the Class C dividend (1:1) is a 2-for-1 split in economic terms. Dilution comes only if Class C is issued for cash; diluted shares were 2,573mn in 3Q26 against 2,572mn a year earlier. $bn. Capex includes finance-lease principal (Meta definition). 4Q25 capex, FCF, cash and debt from the 4Q25 call; leases and commitments from the 10-K and 10-Qs. Debt = carrying value of senior notes.
